title: Warm Homes : Local Grant (WH:LG) Whole House Retrofit Scheme
description:
Derbyshire Dales District Council ('the Council') has secured 'Warm Homes: Local Grant' (WH:LG) funding from the Department of Energy Security and Net Zero (DESNZ) through the Midlands Net Zero Hub (MNZH) consortia to improve the energy efficiency of a number of privately owned domestic properties by the end of March 2028 (with the ability to extend into 2030 if further funding is approved).

Following a re-opening of competition under the Nottingham City Council's, Energy Efficient Retrofit Installers, Dynamic Purchasing System (CPU 7220), Category 7 Whole House Retrofit, the Council have awarded a contract for a main  contractor to carry out a programme of whole-house retrofits using a fabric first approach to install energy efficiency measures and/or low carbon heating measures (excluding fossil fuels) to improve the Standard Assessment Procedure score (SAP) of a number  (target of 48 until March 2028) domestic properties located within the District.
The scope includes the following essential elements:

•	Retrofit Assessments and Technical Surveys by appropriately qualified person, provide evidence of site assessment and documents needed for batching (RdSAP10, IOE, profile, quote and signed customer approval of proposal) 

•	Install approved measures to PAS2035:2023 standards and provide certificates of MCS, Quality Mark, materials and workmanship certificates, insurance backed guarantees, TrustMark certificate, IAA guarantees and pulse/air pressure testing where required) 

•	Post EPC assessment and certificate provided along with post install photo evidence 

•	Measures all TrustMark lodged within deadlines

The contract has been awarded for an initial value of £1,130,000 to cover the Warm Homes: Local Grant installations, which must be completed by 31st March 2028 and reporting finalised by 28th April 2028.

Subject to the Contractor's satisfactory performance, and the Council successfully being awarded further funding, the Council may at its unfettered discretion extend the contract to deliver further installations under future energy efficiency schemes up to the end of March 2030 (or scheme specific deadlines if WH:LG is extended, renamed, rebranded or launched under a difference guise from the government).

title: Ashbourne Airfield Masterplan
description:
Derbyshire Dales District Council (the Council) has awarded a contract following a further competition tender exercise under the Homes England, Development and Regeneration Technical Services (DARTS) Framework Lot 2 - Place making, master planning and design services

The contract is for consultants to provide a comprehensive Masterplan for the Ashbourne Airfield site that will shape the development of the whole site, owned by two private landowners. The commission will be undertaken in 2 stages:

Stage 1 will establish a set of overarching principles for the development of the site. The emerging principles will be agreed with the Council, landowners and other stakeholders. The output from Stage 1 will be a comprehensive report which justifies the overarching development principles for the whole site and how they take account of the ten characteristics of a well-designed place as set out in the National Design Guide.

Stage 2 will be a masterplan for the whole site. This will require the appointed consultants to undertake any and all required site analysis including desktop assessments and reporting, including considering the issues, risks, impacts on holding and development. It will be accompanied by comprehensive development framework which clearly sets out the data and justification that underpins the consultant's recommendations for all the elements of the brief, as well the financial viability of the development.

 The initial contract period for Stage 1 is approx. 3 months; the contract is estimated to commence 1 August 2024 and expire 31 October 2024.

The Council will reserve the option to extend the contract for a further period of 3 months to 31 January 2025 to carry out stage 2 of the project.

title: Local Plan Development Options, Traffic and Transportation Assessment and Flood Risk Assessment (L2 SFRA)
description:
A contract has been awarded following a call off by re-opening competition under the Homes England, Development and Regeneration Technical Services (DARTS) Framework 2023-2027, Lot 1 - end-to-end technical and professional services.

The overall objective of the commission is consultancy services to provide advice to the Council on whether in practical terms there is any realistic prospects that the level of residential development identified as being necessary to meet its future growth aspirations can be delivered, and in a way which will achieve the objectives of delivering sustainable development. 

The requirements are 

Provide advice to support the delivery of the Government's revised housing targets through the identification of sustainable options for the development of communities within the Derbyshire Dales local planning authority area for the period up to 2045

Provide evidence relating to traffic and transportation to support the emerging Derbyshire Dales Local Plan

Undertake a Level 2 Strategic Flood Risk Assessment to assess the cumulative effects of potential development sites within the defined High Sensitive Catchment to assess how the cumulative effects of development sites could impact peak flows, the duration of flooding and timing of flood peaks on receiving watercourses. 

The initial contract period is 12 months.  There will be an option to extend the contract for 12 months, subject to satisfactory performance and business needs. Maximum contract period is two years.

title: Decarbonisation works Northwood Depot
description:
A contract has been awarded for the decarbonisation of  the District Council's Northwood Depot, Harrison Way, Matlock, DE4 2LF, including:

-	Supply and installation of Air Source Heat Pump (ASHP)
-	ASHP siting and protection (plinth and reflective bollards)
-	Alterations of and connection to existing space heating 
-	Flushing and dosing
-	New heating controls
-	Thermal insulation to all pipework and valves, including weatherproofing to external pipework
-	All BWIC
-	Supply and installation of new hot water cylinder and alteration of connections
-	Install new mineral wool fire retardant insulation above mezzanine ceiling
-	Removal of existing and installation of new LED suspended light fittings and associated fittings and controls and all associated works

The project is part of the Public Sector Decarbonisation Scheme   (PSDS) Project 3C to achieve heat decarbonisation and improve energy efficiency of public sector buildings. 

The award is following a further competition process using the  Added Value Portal t/a PAGABO (acting on behalf of Cumbria, Northumberland, Tyne and Wear NHS Foundation Trust) National Framework for Mechanical and Electrical Solutions, AVP-CNTW-001 Lot 3A Mechanical & Electrical Combined Projects of £50k to £500k in the East Midlands Region.

description:

title: To undertake maintenance and aftercare of planted saplings for the LIFE in the Ravines Project (LIFE19/NAT/UK/000147) in the Wye Valley, Derbyshire Dales
description: Provide a service to perform aftercare on planted saplings in ravines woodland of the Derbyshire Dales.  The work involves  removal of weeds and re-planting dead saplings and replacing damaged tree stakes and shelters.  Materials, induing saplings to be provided by the Authority.  The work is on steep remote terrain in the ravine valleys of the Wye Valley in the Derbyshire Dales.  There are approximately 10,400 saplings to be inspected spread across 3 different valleys within the Derbyshire Dales.
